exposure: change in gestational diabetes (GDM) screening policy from risk-factor based to comprehensive screening
cohort: The study included GDM women with singleton pregnancies giving birth in Finland in 2006 (before policy change, n=5185) and 2010 (after policy change, n=6683), along with all other women without pre-pregnancy diabetes in those years (51,759 and 52,398 respectively) as controls.
finding: The shift to comprehensive GDM screening led to a significant increase in the total prevalence of GDM, primarily of diet-treated cases, and identified GDM women who were more often primiparous and had a lower pre-pregnancy BMI.
mod_finding: The overall caesarean section rate remained stable, but it increased among women with GDM from 20.8% to 22.1% during comprehensive screening (adjusted OR 1.22).
cross-section timing: Data was collected for the years 2006 (before policy change) and 2010 (after policy change).
